section: B.3 Data comes in many shapes
text:
B.3 Data comes in many shapes
Prompt 3.1 — read a CSV safely

Read fmcg_sell_out.csv with readr. Show the column types readr guessed. Then read it again forcing every column to text, and explain why a bronze layer might prefer all-text. Show how many values in units_sold are blank, and what blank becomes under each approach.

Prompt 3.2 — tame a presentation spreadsheet

regional_report.xlsx has 4 title rows, region typed once per block (merged cells), one column per month, values as text like “₦149,023,348”, an “All depots” total row and a footnote. Turn it into a tidy table (region, depot, month as a real date in 2025, revenue_ngn as a number). Drop the total and the footnote. Then check: does the sum of depots equal the “All depots” row for January?

Prompt 3.3 — why Parquet?

Convert fmcg_sell_out.csv to Parquet using DuckDB’s COPY command. Compare file sizes and the time to compute total revenue by depot from each. Explain the result in terms of row versus column storage.

Prompt 3.4 — data inventory

List every data file in data/raw with its size, modified date, row count (for CSVs) and an Message-Digest Algorithm 5 (MD5) hash. Flag exact duplicates. Explain why hashing beats comparing file names.

title: Appendix B — Prompt library
text:
B.4 Profile before you trust
Prompt 4.1 — profile in one line

Use DuckDB’s SUMMARIZE to profile fmcg_sell_out.csv. Show column type, min, max, approximate distinct count, null percentage and mean. Then tell me in plain English the three most suspicious things in the output.

Prompt 4.2 — duplicate hunting

For fmcg_sell_out.csv, count (a) exact duplicate rows and (b) duplicate business keys (week_starting, depot_code, sku). For fmcg_depots.csv, find any depot_code that appears more than once and show those rows.

Prompt 4.3 — a reusable profiler

Write an R function profile_table(con, source_sql) that returns one row per column: type, % null, distinct count, min, max, and the three most frequent values. Run it on hr_attrition.csv.

title: Appendix B — Prompt library
section: B.5 SQL: the language of the warehouse
text:
B.5 SQL: the language of the warehouse
Prompt 5.1 — have AI write SQL, then check it

Using DuckDB SQL on table gold.v_sales (columns: week_starting, depot_code, sku, units_sold, revenue_ngn, gross_profit_ngn, on_promotion, discount_pct, stockout_flag, depot_name, region, state, product_name, category, pack_size, year, quarter, year_month), write a query for “gross margin % by category and region for 2025, ranked within each region”. Use a common table expression (CTE) and a window function. Then list the assumptions you made.

title: Appendix B — Prompt library
section: B.6 Bronze: land everything, change nothing
text:
B.6 Bronze: land everything, change nothing
Prompt 6.1 — bronze ingestion with lineage

Create a DuckDB warehouse with schemas bronze, silver, gold and ops. Write a function that loads a CSV into bronze. with every column as VARCHAR, and adds _source_file, _source_system and _loaded_at. Log each load (layer, table, row count) into ops.run_log. Load fmcg_sell_out.csv and show the lineage columns.

Prompt 6.2 — incremental loads with a manifest

Write ingest_increment(con, path, table) that (1) computes the file’s MD5, (2) skips it if ops.load_manifest already has that hash, (3) otherwise creates the bronze table on first load or appends with INSERT … BY NAME so new or re-ordered columns don’t break it, and (4) records the hash, file, rows and time in the manifest. Demonstrate with two deliveries of sell-out data, re-running the first to prove idempotency, and make the second delivery contain an extra column.

Prompt 6.3 — official statistics into bronze

Using R/open_data.R, pull World Bank World Development Indicators (WDI) indicators (gross domestic product (GDP) growth, inflation, GDP per capita, unemployment, remittances as % of GDP) and International Monetary Fund (IMF) World Economic Outlook series (real GDP growth, inflation, government debt) for Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa, Egypt and Côte d’Ivoire, plus Nigeria’s 2023 exports by partner from United Nations (UN) Comtrade. Land them in bronze with their source as lineage. Then show where the World Bank and the IMF disagree about Nigeria’s inflation, and which IMF years are projections.

title: Appendix B — Prompt library
text:
B.7 Silver: clean, conform, remember
Prompt 7.1 — the silver sell-out table

Write DuckDB SQL that builds silver.sell_out from bronze.fmcg_sell_out (all VARCHAR). Cast every column to its proper type. Treat blank units_sold and revenue_ngn as 0, because a blank means a stockout week (rule from the board pack Notes sheet), but keep a boolean units_was_blank as evidence. Keep exactly one row per (week_starting, depot_code, sku), preferring the earliest-loaded row. Comment every business rule.

Prompt 7.2 — slowly changing dimension (SCD) type 2

bronze.fmcg_depots lists DP04 twice (a rename). Build silver.depot_history as an SCD type 2 table: one row per depot version, ordered by load order, with valid_from (the opened date for version 1; 2025-10-01 for later versions, per a business confirmation), valid_to (the day before the next version starts) and is_current.

Prompt 7.3 — conform supplier codes

supply_chain_pos.csv has SUP-CEDAR and SUP-CEDAR-NG, which procurement confirms are the same supplier. Create a small mapping table (source_code → conformed_code, reason, approved_by) and build silver.purchase_orders with a conformed supplier_id. Show on-time delivery % before and after conforming.

title: Appendix B — Prompt library
text:
B.8 Gold: model for decisions
Prompt 8.1 — a star schema from silver

From silver.sell_out, silver.products and silver.depot_history, build a star schema in gold: dim_product (with list margin), dim_depot (current version only), dim_week (year, quarter, year_month, International Organization for Standardization (ISO) week), and fct_sales at grain week × depot × stock-keeping unit (SKU) with gross_profit_ngn = revenue − units × unit cost. Then create a wide view gold.v_sales that pre-joins the star for business intelligence (BI) tools and the semantic layer, and a mart of revenue by depot and month.

Prompt 8.2 — accumulating snapshot

Using silver.purchase_orders (built in Chapter 7), build gold.fct_po_lifecycle with one row per purchase order (PO): order date, received date, promised vs actual lead days, a delivery status (on time / late / date error), and the lateness in days. Then show on-time % and average lateness by conformed supplier.

title: Appendix B — Prompt library
section: B.9 Tests and the publish gate
text:
B.9 Tests and the publish gate
Prompt 9.1 — a test suite for gold

Write data tests for the retail gold layer: uniqueness of fct_sales at its grain and of each dimension key; not-null revenue; units ≥ 0; discount between 0 and 0.5; on_promotion in (0,1); fact-to-dimension relationships; at least 50,000 rows; freshness within 21 days of a given as-of date (warning only); and financial year 2025 (FY2025) revenue reconciling to the Excel regional report within 1% for every depot. Return a results table and log it.

title: Appendix B — Prompt library
section: B.10 The semantic layer: one definition of every KPI
text:
B.10 The semantic layer: one definition of every KPI
Prompt 10.1 — compile and query

Using my metrics.yml and the metric_sql() compiler in kit.R, generate SQL for revenue, gross margin % and stockout rate by region and by quarter for 2025. Print the SQL, run it, and chart revenue by region over quarters.

Prompt 10.2 — price-volume bridge

Using the semantic layer’s units and avg_selling_price metrics, decompose the change in revenue between Q4 2024 and Q4 2025 for each category into a volume effect and a price effect (with an interaction term), and show the bridge as a table.

title: Appendix B — Prompt library
section: B.11 Vector search and AI on governed data
text:
B.11 Vector search and AI on governed data
Prompt 11.1 — vector index for complaints

Build a vector index over silver.complaints.complaint_text using the kit’s vector_index() (term frequency–inverse document frequency (TF-IDF)), storing vectors as DOUBLE[] in DuckDB. Then search for “I can’t see my Retirement Savings Account (RSA) balance online” and “my employer did not remit my contribution”, and show the top five matches with similarity scores.

Prompt 11.2 — discover complaint themes

Cluster the complaint vectors into 8 themes with k-means. For each cluster, show its size, its most characteristic words, its share of Pidgin complaints and its average days to resolve. Name each theme in plain English.

Prompt 11.3 — a governed retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) prompt

Build a function that, for a question, retrieves the 8 most similar complaints and assembles a prompt instructing the model to answer only from those complaints, cite complaint identifiers (IDs), say “not enough evidence” if they don’t answer it, and never output personal data. Show the assembled prompt; call Claude only if ANTHROPIC_application programming interface (API)_KEY is set.

Prompt 11.4 — evaluate text-to-SQL

Build a small evaluation harness: a table of golden questions, each with a reference SQL. For each candidate SQL (from any model), run both, compare the results (same rows and values within 0.1%), and report accuracy. Include one deliberately wrong candidate to prove the harness catches it.

title: Appendix B — Prompt library
section: B.12 Serving: trusted data where people work
text:
B.12 Serving: trusted data where people work
Prompt 12.1 — publish a serving mart

After the tests pass, publish gold.dim_depot, gold.dim_product, gold.dim_week, gold.fct_sales and gold.mart_depot_month to a SQLite file, atomically (build to a temp file, then swap). Add a view in the SQLite file that pre-joins the star for Excel users. Then prove a reader sees the right totals.

title: Appendix B — Prompt library
section: B.13 Dashboards with Quarto and Shiny
text:
B.13 Dashboards with Quarto and Shiny
Prompt 13.1 — design critique

Here is a screenshot of my dashboard [attach]. Critique it against these principles: one decision per page, Z-pattern reading order, comparisons on every key performance indicator (KPI), definitions on hover, visible freshness and test status, accessible colour, and speed. Give the five highest-impact changes in priority order.

title: Appendix B — Prompt library
section: B.14 Operations: run it every day without you
text:
B.14 Operations: run it every day without you
Prompt 14.1 — a robust pipeline runner

Write run_platform() for my retail pipeline. It should: build into a temporary DuckDB file so the live warehouse is never half-built; time each step and log it; retry the ingest step up to 3 times with a back-off; run the tests; swap the new warehouse in only if the gate passes; otherwise keep the old file and raise an alert; and return a one-line status summary. Make it safe to run twice at the same time with a lock file.

Prompt 14.2 — write the runbook

Write a one-page runbook for the nightly retail platform refresh: what it does, schedule and service-level agreement (SLA), how to tell it failed, the five most likely failures with diagnosis and fix steps (source file late, schema drift, test failure, disk full, lock left behind), how to re-run safely, how to backfill a past week, and who to escalate to.

title: Appendix B — Prompt library
text:
B.15 Security, privacy and governance
Prompt 15.1 — a personally identifiable information (PII) scanner

Write a function that scans every VARCHAR column of every table in a DuckDB schema and flags columns where more than 5% of a sample of values look like Nigerian phone numbers, email addresses, 11-digit identifiers (possible Bank Verification Number (BVN) or National Identification Number (NIN)), or personal names from a short list. Output a classification suggestion per column for the steward to confirm.

title: Appendix B — Prompt library
text:
B.16 Playbook: Human resources
Prompt 17.1 — human resources (HR) pipeline

Build an HR pipeline with the kit’s run_pipeline(): bronze from hr_attrition.csv; silver.employees typed, with exit_interview_booked excluded because it leaks the outcome; gold.fct_employee with a compa-ratio (pay ÷ median pay for the grade), an engagement band and a promotion-wait band; and a department mart. Tests: unique employee_id, engagement 1–5, pay > 0, accepted grades and work patterns. Publish the mart to a serving SQLite file.

Prompt 17.2 — prove the leakage

Fit two logistic regressions for left_within_12m: one with exit_interview_booked (from bronze), one without (from gold). Compare their area under the curve (AUC) on a 30% hold-out. Explain to an HR director why the “better” model is useless.

title: Appendix B — Prompt library
section: B.17 Playbook: Retail chains and FMCG
text:
B.17 Playbook: Retail chains and FMCG
Prompt 20.1 — promo uplift

Using gold.v_sales, estimate promotion uplift: for each category, compare average units per depot-SKU-week on promotion vs off promotion, within the same depot and SKU, so that big depots don’t bias the result. Then compute the incremental gross profit after discount. Which categories’ promotions pay for themselves?

Prompt 20.2 — read an A/B test properly

Analyse ab_test_checkout.csv (arm, device, converted, revenue_ngn). First check for sample-ratio mismatch (SRM) against the intended 50/50 split, overall and by device, with a chi-square test. Only then compare conversion and revenue per user between arms with confidence intervals. Explain why SRM invalidates the naive result.

title: Appendix B — Prompt library
text:
B.18 Capstone: prove mastery
Prompt 26.1 — architecture brief

I am building a governed analytics platform for [decision] at [organisation] in [sector]. My sources are [list, with format and owner]. Using the six-layer architecture (sources, ingest, bronze/silver/gold warehouse, test gate, govern, serve, plus the operations and security plane), draft a one-page brief: the decision and its owner, the grain of the main fact table, the dimensions, ten data tests (including one reconciliation), eight semantic-layer metrics with owners, the serving targets by audience, and the top five privacy and operational risks.

Prompt 26.2 — red-team my platform

Act as an internal auditor and a sceptical chief financial officer (CFO). Here is my platform’s design and test results [paste]. Find the five most serious ways a wrong number could still reach a decision-maker, and for each, the control that would stop it.

title: Appendix C — Troubleshooting
text:
Symptom
Likely cause
Fix




IO Error: Could not set lock on file ... .duckdb
Another R session (or the dashboard) has the warehouse open for writing
Close other sessions; open readers with read_only = TRUE; build to a temp file and swap (Chapter 14)


DuckDB file won’t open after copying to another machine
It was created by a newer DuckDB version than the one installed
install.packages("duckdb") to update, or re-run the pipeline to rebuild the file


Extension Autoloading Error (json, postgres, vss)
DuckDB downloads extensions on first use; the network or proxy blocked it
Allow extensions.duckdb.org, or INSTALL json; LOAD json; once on a connected machine; or use an R alternative (jsonlite)


₦ or accented letters show as ? or â‚¦
File saved in an encoding other than Unicode Transformation Format, 8-bit (UTF-8) (Excel’s CSV (Comma delimited) option)
Save as CSV UTF-8 instead; or readr::read_csv(f, locale = locale(encoding = "latin1"))


Numbers read as text in Excel imports
Values stored as text, with commas or currency symbols
readr::parse_number() in R or regexp_replace + CAST in Structured Query Language (SQL) (Chapter 7)


Totals are higher than Finance’s
A join fan-out from a duplicated dimension key, or duplicate loads
Run uniqueness tests on every dimension key; check _source_file counts in bronze


Dashboard doesn’t update after a rebuild
The app holds an old connection, or there’s no reactivePoll
Open short-lived connections per query; watch the file’s modified time (Chapter 13)


quarto serve says the port is in use
A previous app is still running
quarto serve 02-dashboard.qmd --port 7788, or stop the old R process


Shiny dashboard works locally but not when deployed
Absolute paths, missing packages, or secrets not set on the server
Use project-relative paths and config.yml; record packages with renv; set environment variables in the host’s settings


SQL works in DuckDB but fails on PostgreSQL
Dialect differences (QUALIFY, GROUP BY ALL, date_trunc arguments)
Use a common table expression (CTE) + row_number() instead of QUALIFY; list the GROUP BY columns; check the function docs


Test passes, but the number is still wrong
No test covers that failure mode
Add a reconciliation test against an external source; ask “what would have caught this?” after every incident


Artificial intelligence (AI)-written SQL returns plausible but wrong results
Wrong grain, missing filter, average of ratios, unbounded dates
Review with the Chapter 5 checklist; add the case to your golden-question set (Chapter 11)


Git wants to commit a 200 megabytes (MB) file
Data or databases in the repository
Add data/db/, *.duckdb and *.sqlite to .gitignore; remove them from the index with git rm --cached

title: Appendix D — Official and open data catalogue
section: D.3 Rules of the road for external data
text:
D.3 Rules of the road for external data

Name the source on every chart and table. “₦/US$ (CBN official)” is a different number from a parallel-market rate.
Keep vintages. Official figures are revised. Store the pull date with the data, so a board pack can be reproduced exactly as it was presented.
Separate actuals from projections. IMF WEO mixes both; keep a flag, and let the semantic layer enforce it.
Mind breaks in series. Rebasings (Nigeria’s GDP in 2014, CPI in 2025) mean a chart can show a jump that is a methodology change, not an event.
Check the licence. Most multilateral data is open (Creative Commons (CC) BY 4.0 for the World Bank). Some datasets restrict redistribution. Record the licence in the catalogue.
Cache, then test freshness. APIs change and go down. The Lab’s with_cache() keeps the last good pull, and a freshness test tells you when it is too old.







🧠 Prompt D.1 — wire a new provider in




I want to add [provider] data on [indicator] for [countries, years] to my warehouse. Write a function in the style of R/open_data.R that returns the standard tidy columns (source, dataset, indicator, indicator_name, iso3, country, year, value), caches each pull to data/open/, and falls back to the cache when the API fails. Then write two data tests for it: a freshness test and a plausibility range for the values.

title: Appendix F — DIY prompt book: from your raw data to a live dashboard
text:
F.1 How to use this prompt book
This appendix is a hands-on, do-it-yourself guide. You have data of all sorts in your organisation: spreadsheets on shared drives, exports from an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system, a customer relationship management (CRM) database, a web service or two. You want a live, interactive dashboard that people trust. This prompt book takes you there in fourteen stages. Each stage gives you:
It is built on a starter kit: a ready-made project folder in which every layer of the architecture already works. You don’t write a pipeline engine or a dashboard from scratch. You write the parts that are specific to your organisation: what the data means, how to clean it, what to measure. Those are exactly the parts an AI assistant can help with, and that a person must check.

F.1.1 The loop at every stage





flowchart LR
  A["🧠 Prompt<br/>(attach ai_context.md)"] --> B["Paste the answer<br/>into the named file"]
  B --> C["▶ Run<br/>run_pipeline.R --to=stage"]
  C --> D{"✔ Check"}
  D -- "wrong" --> A
  D -- "right" --> E["💾 Commit"]
  E --> F["Next stage"]







Prompt. Start every AI session with the session primer (below), then the stage’s prompt. Attach ai_context.md, which the kit rewrites on every run. It describes every table (columns, types, null %, ranges) without sending a single full record.
Paste the answer into the file the prompt names. The AI writes files; you place them.
Run the stage. Every run starts again from the raw data, so you can run as often as you like.
Check against the stage’s ✔ list. If something is wrong, paste the error or the surprising number back to the AI with “this is what I got; what is wrong?”.
Commit when the check passes, so you can always go back.



F.1.2 Rehearse on the practice organisation first
The kit includes Trans-Sahel Distribution Ltd, the book’s running example. It has sources in every shape you will meet: a comma-separated values (CSV) sell-out file with re-sent rows, a “presentation” Excel report, a JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) export, a database and a web application programming interface (API) (see practice/README.md).

title: Appendix F — DIY prompt book: from your raw data to a live dashboard
section: F.2 The session primer (paste at the start of every AI session)
text:
F.2 The session primer (paste at the start of every AI session)
AI assistants forget everything between sessions. This primer tells the assistant what the kit is, what it may assume and how to answer. Paste it first, every time, then attach ai_context.md.






🧠 Prompt F0 — session primer




I am building a governed analytics platform with a starter kit. Data flows one way: files and systems land in bronze (DuckDB, every column as delivered, with lineage columns _source_file, _row and _loaded_at); Structured Query Language (SQL) files in sql/silver/ clean and type them; SQL files in sql/gold/ model them for decisions; tests/tests.yml holds data tests that must pass before anything is published; semantic/metrics.yml defines every metric once, and a Quarto + Shiny dashboard reads only those definitions.
The attached ai_context.md describes every table: columns, types, null %, approximate distinct counts and ranges. It is all you know about the data. Never invent a table or a column that is not in it; if you need one, say so.
When you write code: use DuckDB SQL; return complete files, each starting with a comment giving its path (for example -- sql/silver/03_sell_out.sql); use CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE (or VIEW); comment every business rule in plain English; and finish with the assumptions you made and the questions I should ask a data owner. If my request is ambiguous, ask me before writing code. My organisation: [[one line: who you are and what the dashboard is for]].
crumbs: F  DIY prompt book: from your raw data to a live dashboard

title: Appendix F — DIY prompt book: from your raw data to a live dashboard
text:
F.3 Stage 0 · Install your workbench
🎯 Goal: R, Quarto, an editor and Git installed, and the kit’s checks all OK.

Install R (4.3 or newer) from cran.r-project.org, Quarto from quarto.org, and Git from git-scm.com.
Install an editor: Positron (positron.posit.co) or RStudio. Positron includes an AI assistant pane; any assistant you are allowed to use works.
Unzip the starter kit, rename the folder, open it in the editor and, in its terminal, run:

Rscript 00_setup.R






🧠 Prompt F0.1 — fix an installation problem




I am setting up R and Quarto on [[Windows 11 / macOS 14 / Ubuntu 24.04]], on a [[company-managed / personal]] laptop [[behind a proxy / without admin rights]]. Running Rscript 00_setup.R gave this output: [[paste the output]]. Explain what is wrong in plain language and give me the exact steps to fix it, one at a time, without needing admin rights if possible.



✔ Check. Every line of the --- checks --- block says OK. (The optional database drivers matter only if you will pull from PostgreSQL, SQL Server or Oracle.)
💾 Commit. git init, then git add -A and git commit -m "Start from the DIY starter kit". The kit’s .gitignore already keeps data, secrets and generated files out of Git.

title: Appendix F — DIY prompt book: from your raw data to a live dashboard
section: F.4 Stage 1 · Create the project and write the brief
text:
F.4 Stage 1 · Create the project and write the brief
🎯 Goal: one page that says who the dashboard is for, which decisions it supports, and which numbers matter.
Most dashboard projects fail here, not in the code. A clear brief tells you which sources you need, what “correct” means, and when you are done. The kit copies brief.md to the top of ai_context.md, so every later prompt knows your situation.






🧠 Prompt F1 — interview me for the brief




Interview me to fill in brief.md for a dashboard project. Ask me one question at a time and wait for my answer: the organisation and unit; the decisions the dashboard must support (and how often they are made); the audience; the three to six numbers that matter, each with the person who owns its definition; the breakdowns people ask for; the time grain; the authoritative totals the numbers must reconcile to (for example a finance report); and whether any personal data is involved. Push back if a “number that matters” has no owner or no decision attached to it. At the end, write the complete brief.md in the same bullet format as the template I paste below. [[paste the brief.md template]]



Then set your project’s name in config.yml (project:) and the title at the top of dashboard.qmd.
✔ Check. Every line of brief.md is filled in. Each key number has an owner and a decision. You can name the report you will reconcile to. If personal data is involved, set ai_context_samples: false in config.yml now (Stage 13 explains why).






📗 Reference answer (practice organisation)







practice/brief.md

- **Organisation and unit:** Trans-Sahel Distribution Ltd (practice organisation), Commercial Finance
- **The decisions this dashboard supports:** the weekly depot performance review; promotion planning; stockout follow-up
- **Audience:** regional managers (weekly), CFO and Commercial Director (monthly)
- **The 3–6 numbers that matter (with owners):** revenue (CFO), gross margin % (CFO), units sold (Commercial Director), stockout rate (Head of Supply Chain), promotion share of revenue (Head of Trade Marketing)
- **Breakdowns people ask for:** region, depot, product category, product
- **Time grain:** weekly (sell-out arrives weekly), reviewed monthly
- **Authoritative totals to reconcile to:** Commercial Finance's FY2025 regional report (revenue by depot and month)
- **Data protection notes:** no personal data in scope (depot- and product-level sales only)




💾 Commit: "Brief and project settings".

title: Appendix F — DIY prompt book: from your raw data to a live dashboard
section: F.5 Stage 2 · Land your files in bronze
text:
F.5 Stage 2 · Land your files in bronze
🎯 Goal: every file the dashboard needs, loaded into bronze exactly as delivered, with lineage.

Collect exports, don’t edit them. Ask each owner for the regular export (the one that could be produced again next month), not a hand-tidied copy. Keep originals as they arrive.
Drop them into data/raw/, one sub-folder per source (for example data/raw/sales/, data/raw/finance/). The kit reads CSV, tab-separated values (TSV), Excel (every sheet), Parquet and JSON.
Only what the brief needs. If a file holds personal data the brief doesn’t need, ask for an export without those columns. That is data minimisation, and it is easier than deleting later.
Run:

Rscript run_pipeline.R --to=bronze
Each file becomes one table, bronze.<file name> (an Excel workbook with several sheets gives one table per sheet, bronze.<file>__<sheet>), and the run lists each with its row count. Open ai_context.md to see what landed.
Spreadsheets made for printing usually land wrongly the first time: title rows become the header, so columns are called ...2 and ...3. Fix that with read options in sources.yml, not by editing the file.






🧠 Prompt F2 — fix how files were read




[[Session primer, then attach ai_context.md.]] Look at every bronze table. Which ones look as if they were read wrongly: a title row used as the header (columns named like ...2), the wrong delimiter (everything in one column), a broken encoding (â‚¦ instead of ₦), several tables on one sheet, or notes rows mixed with data? For each, write the files: entry for sources.yml that fixes it (options: skip, header, delim, encoding, sheets, table, skip_file), and tell me what to ask the owner if the file cannot be fixed by read options alone.



✔ Check.

Every file you dropped in appears in the run output with a sensible row count. (Compare with the row count you see when you open the file.)
Column names in ai_context.md match the files’ real headers.
ERROR lines name a file and a reason: fix the read option or ask for a cleaner export.







📗 Reference answer (practice organisation)





Finance’s regional report has four title rows above the header, so it needs skip: 4. The other files land correctly as they are. The files: section of sources.yml (full file in Stage 3):
files:
  "finance/regional_report.xlsx":
    skip: 4



💾 Commit: "Land raw files in bronze" (the data itself stays out of Git; the read options go in).

title: Appendix F — DIY prompt book: from your raw data to a live dashboard
section: F.6 Stage 3 · Connect databases and web APIs
text:
F.6 Stage 3 · Connect databases and web APIs
🎯 Goal: system data pulled straight from the source, on every run, with no manual exports.
sources.yml lists databases (SQLite, DuckDB, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server, Oracle or others through Open Database Connectivity (ODBC)) and web APIs (JSON or CSV). Passwords and tokens go in .Renviron; sources.yml only holds the names of those variables. API responses are cached, so a failed call falls back to the last good copy.






Asking information technology (IT) for access: what to request



A read-only account; access to a view or a reporting replica rather than live production tables; the host, port, database name and driver; and the time window when queries are allowed. Ask for exactly the tables in your brief. You are much more likely to get a quick yes.








🧠 Prompt F3 — write the source entries




[[Session primer.]] Write sources.yml entries for these sources. Database: [[system name, e.g. our SQL Server ERP]], driver [[sqlite / postgres / odbc]], connection facts [[host, port, database, data source name (DSN), without any password]], and I need [[tables or a query: e.g. invoices since 2024 with these columns…]]. Web API: [[uniform resource locator (URL) and documentation link]], authentication [[none / API key in a header / bearer token]], response format [[JSON / CSV]]. Reference every secret by a variable name for .Renviron and show me the .Renviron lines with empty values. If a query could pull millions of rows, add a date filter and tell me why.



Then fill in .Renviron (restart R after editing) and run Rscript run_pipeline.R --to=bronze again.
✔ Check. Each source appears as bronze.<name>_<table> with a row count you can confirm with the system owner. Re-run it: the counts are the same, because every run rebuilds from the sources. No password appears in any file you would commit (git status should not list .Renviron).






📗 Reference answer (practice organisation)





The depot master comes from the ERP database, and Nigeria’s inflation comes from the World Bank’s open API (see Appendix D for International Monetary Fund (IMF), United Nations (UN) Comtrade, United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) and Nigerian sources):


practice/sources.yml

# Practice organisation: Trans-Sahel Distribution Ltd (reference answer for Stage 3)
files:
  "finance/regional_report.xlsx":
    skip: 4                    # four title rows above the header (Chapter 3)

databases:
  - name: erp
    driver: sqlite
    path: data/systems/erp.sqlite
    tables: [depots]

apis:
  - name: wb_inflation_nga
    url: "https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/NGA/indicator/FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG?format=json&per_page=100"
    format: json
    pick: 2                    # World Bank returns [metadata, data]: keep the data




💾 Commit: "Pull from ERP and World Bank".

title: Appendix F — DIY prompt book: from your raw data to a live dashboard
section: F.7 Stage 4 · Profile before you trust
text:
F.7 Stage 4 · Profile before you trust
🎯 Goal: a written list of every data problem, with the rule that fixes it and the person who must agree to that rule.
This stage writes no code. It’s the conversation that makes silver possible. The AI spots patterns in ai_context.md; the data owners decide what they mean.






🧠 Prompt F4 — the issues log




[[Session primer, then attach ai_context.md.]] Profile every bronze table against the six quality dimensions: completeness, uniqueness, validity, consistency, timeliness and accuracy. Look especially for: likely duplicate keys; blanks that might mean something (zero, not applicable, still open); numbers or dates stored with symbols or in mixed formats; codes that differ between tables for the same thing; one entity appearing twice (a rename, a merger, two spellings); periods that don’t overlap between sources; and columns that could leak an outcome. Write docs/issues.md as a table: table, column, issue, evidence from ai_context.md, proposed rule, who must confirm it. Then list the SQL checks I should run to confirm each suspicion.



Run the suggested checks (in Positron, open data/db/dev.duckdb with the database pane, or in R DBI::dbGetQuery()), then take the issues log to the owners. Their answers become the comments in your silver SQL.
✔ Check. Every issue has evidence and an owner. Every rule that changes a number (for example “blank units mean a stockout, so 0”) has been confirmed by that owner, in writing.

title: Appendix F — DIY prompt book: from your raw data to a live dashboard
section: F.8 Stage 5 · Silver: clean, type and conform
text:
F.8 Stage 5 · Silver: clean, type and conform
🎯 Goal: one silver table per real-world thing, typed and cleaned by written, agreed rules.
Write one SQL file per silver table, numbered in the order they must run (01_depots.sql, 02_products.sql, …). Each file reads only bronze (or earlier silver) tables.






🧠 Prompt F5 — a silver table




[[Session primer, then attach ai_context.md and docs/issues.md.]] Write sql/silver/[[NN]]_[[name]].sql that creates silver.[[name]] from bronze.[[table]]. Rules: cast every column to its proper type (use TRY_CAST where values may be dirty and say what becomes null); trim text and standardise codes; apply these agreed rules from the issues log: [[list them]]; keep exactly one row per [[business key]], preferring the first row loaded (QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY _row) = 1); keep an evidence flag wherever a rule changes a value; [[if history matters: build a type 2 history with valid_from, valid_to, is_current]]; [[if some rows can’t be fixed: put them in silver.[[name]]_rejects with a reason column, instead of dropping them]]. Comment each rule with who agreed it. Afterwards, give me two SQL queries that prove the rules worked.



Rscript run_pipeline.R --to=silver
✔ Check.

Each file runs (ok) and the run lists the silver table it created with a row count.
Row counts make sense: silver = bronze − duplicates − quarantined rows. Write the arithmetic down.
The two proof queries from the prompt return what you expect (for example, zero duplicate keys).
An error stops the run and names the file and line. Paste it back to the AI.







📗 Reference answer (practice organisation)





Five files. The sell-out table shows the typical pattern:


practice/sql/silver/03_sell_out.sql

-- silver.sell_out: typed weekly sell-out, one row per week x depot x SKU.
-- Rule (board pack Notes sheet): a blank units_sold means a stockout week -> 0, and we keep the evidence flag.
-- Rule: re-sent rows for the same key collapse to the first one loaded (214 duplicate keys in the source).
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver.sell_out AS
SELECT CAST(week_starting AS DATE)                  AS week_starting,
       trim(depot_code)                             AS depot_code,
       trim(sku)                                    AS sku,
       COALESCE(TRY_CAST(units_sold  AS DOUBLE), 0) AS units_sold,
       TRY_CAST(unit_price_ngn AS DOUBLE)           AS unit_price_ngn,
       CAST(on_promotion  AS INTEGER)               AS on_promotion,
       CAST(discount_pct  AS DOUBLE)                AS discount_pct,
       CAST(stockout_flag AS INTEGER)               AS stockout_flag,
       COALESCE(TRY_CAST(revenue_ngn AS DOUBLE), 0) AS revenue_ngn,
       units_sold IS NULL                           AS units_was_blank
FROM bronze.fmcg_sell_out
QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY week_starting, depot_code, sku ORDER BY _row) = 1;



practice/sql/silver/04_regional_report.sql

-- silver.regional_report: Finance's printed FY2025 Excel report made tidy, for reconciliation.
-- Fill the merged region cells down, drop the "All depots" total and the footnote, unpivot the
-- twelve month columns, and turn "₦149,023,348" into a number.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver.regional_report AS
WITH filled AS (
  SELECT last_value(region IGNORE NULLS) OVER (ORDER BY _row) AS region, depot,
         Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep, Oct, Nov, Dec
  FROM bronze.regional_report
  WHERE depot IS NOT NULL AND depot <> 'All depots'
), long AS (
  UNPIVOT filled ON Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep, Oct, Nov, Dec INTO NAME mon VALUE revenue_txt
)
SELECT region, depot AS depot_name,
       strptime('2025 ' || mon || ' 01', '%Y %b %d')::DATE            AS month,
       CAST(regexp_replace(revenue_txt, '[^0-9.]', '', 'g') AS DOUBLE) AS revenue_ngn
FROM long;

The other three (01_depots.sql, 02_products.sql, 05_marketing_and_macro.sql) are in practice/sql/silver/ in the kit.



💾 Commit: "Silver layer".

title: Appendix F — DIY prompt book: from your raw data to a live dashboard
section: F.9 Stage 6 · Gold: model for decisions
text:
F.9 Stage 6 · Gold: model for decisions
🎯 Goal: facts and dimensions at a declared grain, small marts for spreadsheet users, and one wide view for the dashboard.
First decide the shape; then write it.






🧠 Prompt F6a — design the gold layer




[[Session primer, then attach ai_context.md and brief.md.]] Propose a gold layer for the decisions in my brief. For each fact table, write its grain in one sentence (“one row per … per …”). List the dimensions and which facts use them (a bus matrix). Propose marts for people who will use Excel or Power BI. Finally, define one wide view, gold.v_dashboard, that the dashboard will read: exactly one date column, the breakdown columns from my brief (as text), and the measure columns needed for my key numbers. Warn me about any join that could multiply rows (fan-out). Don’t write SQL yet.









🧠 Prompt F6b — write the gold SQL




Good. Now write the files sql/gold/01_dimensions.sql, 02_[[fact]].sql, 03_v_dashboard.sql and 04_marts.sql for that design, reading only silver tables. Use CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE for facts, dimensions and marts and CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW for gold.v_dashboard. Put the grain sentence as a comment at the top of each fact. Then give me a query that proves gold.v_dashboard has exactly as many rows as the fact table.



Rscript run_pipeline.R --to=gold
✔ Check. gold.v_dashboard has the same row count as its fact table (no fan-out). Its date column really is a date. Its breakdown columns hold the values people use in meetings (names, not codes).






📗 Reference answer (practice organisation)







practice/sql/gold/02_fct_sales.sql

-- Grain: one row per week x depot x SKU (a periodic snapshot fact).
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE gold.fct_sales AS
SELECT s.week_starting, s.depot_code, s.sku,
       s.units_sold, s.revenue_ngn,
       s.revenue_ngn - s.units_sold * p.unit_cost_ngn AS gross_profit_ngn,
       s.on_promotion, s.discount_pct, s.stockout_flag, s.units_was_blank
FROM silver.sell_out s
JOIN silver.products p USING (sku);



practice/sql/gold/03_v_dashboard.sql

-- The one wide view the dashboard and the semantic layer read: the star, pre-joined.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW gold.v_dashboard AS
SELECT f.week_starting, d.region, d.depot_name, p.category, p.product_name,
       f.units_sold, f.revenue_ngn, f.gross_profit_ngn, f.on_promotion, f.discount_pct, f.stockout_flag
FROM gold.fct_sales f
JOIN gold.dim_depot   d USING (depot_code)
JOIN gold.dim_product p USING (sku);

The dimensions and marts are in practice/sql/gold/ in the kit.



💾 Commit: "Gold layer".
crumbs: F  DIY prompt book: from your raw data to a live dashboard

title: Appendix F — DIY prompt book: from your raw data to a live dashboard
text:
F.10 Stage 7 · The publish gate
🎯 Goal: automated tests that stop wrong numbers from ever reaching the dashboard.
Each test in tests/tests.yml counts the rows that break a rule. Zero means PASS. With severity: error (the default), any failure keeps the previous good warehouse live; severity: warn reports but still publishes. The eight types are the ones in Chapter 9: unique, not_null, accepted, range, relationship, fresh, rowcount and custom (any SQL that returns a count).






🧠 Prompt F7 — write the gate




[[Session primer, then attach ai_context.md and brief.md.]] Write tests/tests.yml for my gold layer, using the kit’s test types (unique, not_null, accepted, range, relationship, fresh, rowcount, custom). I need: uniqueness at every fact’s grain and of every dimension key; not-null key measures; plausible ranges ([[e.g. discount 0–50%, quantities ≥ 0]]); accepted codes for [[columns]]; every fact key present in its dimension; a minimum row count; freshness of [[N]] days as a warning; and a custom reconciliation: [[measure]] for [[period]] must match [[authoritative report]] within [[1%]] per [[unit]]. For each test, add a comment saying which failure it catches.



Rscript run_pipeline.R --to=test
✔ Check.

Every test runs and says PASS (or WARN for freshness on old data).
Prove the gate works. Copy a raw file, break one value on purpose (a negative quantity, a duplicated line), run the full pipeline, and watch it refuse to publish: FAIL, an ALERT line, and warehouse.failed.duckdb kept for inspection. Restore the file and run again.
If the reconciliation fails on real data, don’t loosen it. Find out why. It is the most valuable test you have.







📗 Reference answer (practice organisation)







practice/tests/tests.yml

# Practice organisation: the publish gate (reference answer for Stage 7)
- {type: unique,       table: gold.fct_sales,   columns: [week_starting, depot_code, sku]}
- {type: unique,       table: gold.dim_depot,   columns: [depot_code]}
- {type: unique,       table: gold.dim_product, columns: [sku]}
- {type: not_null,     table: gold.fct_sales,   column: revenue_ngn}
- {type: range,        table: gold.fct_sales,   column: units_sold,   min: 0}
- {type: range,        table: gold.fct_sales,   column: discount_pct, min: 0, max: 0.5}
- {type: accepted,     table: gold.fct_sales,   column: on_promotion, values: ["0", "1"]}
- {type: relationship, table: gold.fct_sales,   column: depot_code, ref_table: gold.dim_depot}
- {type: relationship, table: gold.fct_sales,   column: sku,        ref_table: gold.dim_product}
- {type: rowcount,     table: gold.fct_sales,   min: 50000}
# The practice data ends in March 2026, so freshness is measured against a fixed date.
# With your own data, delete the as_of line so it is measured against today.
- {type: fresh, table: gold.fct_sales, column: week_starting, max_days: 21, as_of: "2026-04-14", severity: warn}
- type: custom
  name: "reconcile: FY2025 revenue by depot vs Finance's regional report (within 1%)"
  sql: |
    WITH xl AS (SELECT h.depot_code, SUM(r.revenue_ngn) AS xl
                FROM silver.regional_report r
                JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT depot_code, depot_name FROM silver.depot_history) h USING (depot_name)
                GROUP BY 1),
         wh AS (SELECT depot_code, SUM(revenue_ngn) AS wh FROM gold.fct_sales
                WHERE year(week_starting) = 2025 GROUP BY 1)
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM xl JOIN wh USING (depot_code) WHERE abs(xl / wh - 1) > 0.01




💾 Commit: "Publish gate".

title: Appendix F — DIY prompt book: from your raw data to a live dashboard
text:
F.11 Stage 8 · The semantic layer
🎯 Goal: every number on the dashboard defined once, with an owner, in semantic/metrics.yml.
The dashboard has no formulas of its own. It reads the model section (which view, which date column, which breakdowns) and the metrics section (one SQL expression per number). Change a definition here and every page, every filter and every export changes with it.






🧠 Prompt F8 — define the metrics




[[Session primer, then attach ai_context.md and brief.md.]] Write semantic/metrics.yml for the kit. In model, set table: gold.v_dashboard, its date column as time, a default grain, and the breakdown columns as dimensions. In metrics, define each key number in my brief as one SQL aggregate over gold.v_dashboard, with label, sql, format (currency, number or pct), owner, status (certified or exploratory) and a one-sentence description. Ratios must be sum first, divide last, with NULLIF to avoid dividing by zero. Mark up to four headline metrics with kpi: true. Then give me one SQL query per metric that recomputes it for [[one month]] directly from the silver tables, so I can check it by hand.



✔ Check. For one month, each metric matches your hand calculation and, for the certified ones, the owner’s own figure. Only metrics the owner has approved are marked certified.






📗 Reference answer (practice organisation)







practice/semantic/metrics.yml

# Practice organisation: the semantic layer (reference answer for Stage 8)
model:
  table: gold.v_dashboard
  time: week_starting
  grain: month
  dimensions: [region, depot_name, category, product_name]
metrics:
  revenue:
    label: Revenue
    sql: SUM(revenue_ngn)
    format: currency
    kpi: true
    owner: CFO
    status: certified
    description: Sell-out revenue in naira after promotional discounts. Reconciles to Finance's regional report within 1%.
  gross_margin_pct:
    label: Gross margin
    sql: 100 * SUM(gross_profit_ngn) / NULLIF(SUM(revenue_ngn), 0)
    format: pct
    kpi: true
    owner: CFO
    status: certified
    description: Gross profit as a share of revenue. Sum first, divide last.
  units:
    label: Units sold
    sql: SUM(units_sold)
    format: number
    kpi: true
    owner: Commercial Director
    status: certified
    description: Units sold. A blank in the source means a stockout week and counts as 0.
  stockout_rate_pct:
    label: Stockout rate
    sql: 100 * AVG(stockout_flag)
    format: pct
    kpi: true
    owner: Head of Supply Chain
    status: certified
    description: Share of depot-SKU-weeks flagged as out of stock.
  promo_share_pct:
    label: Promotion share of revenue
    sql: 100 * SUM(CASE WHEN on_promotion = 1 THEN revenue_ngn END) / NULLIF(SUM(revenue_ngn), 0)
    format: pct
    owner: Head of Trade Marketing
    status: exploratory
    description: Revenue earned on promotion as a share of all revenue.
  avg_selling_price:
    label: Average selling price
    sql: SUM(revenue_ngn) / NULLIF(SUM(units_sold), 0)
    format: currency
    owner: Commercial Director
    status: exploratory
    description: Revenue per unit sold (weighted, not an average of prices).




💾 Commit: "Semantic layer".

section: F.12 Stage 9 · One command: run the whole pipeline
text:
F.12 Stage 9 · One command: run the whole pipeline
🎯 Goal: raw data to a tested, published warehouse with one command, safe to run at any time.
Rscript run_pipeline.R
What happens, in order:

A fresh copy of the warehouse is built from the raw data: bronze, silver, gold.
The tests run. Results are stored in the warehouse and appended to logs/test_history.csv.
Gate open: the new warehouse replaces the live one in a single rename (the atomic swap), and every gold table is copied to data/serve/mart.sqlite for Excel and Power BI users.
Gate closed: nothing changes for users. The failed build is kept as warehouse.failed.duckdb, and an alert goes to logs/alerts.log (and to Teams or Slack, if you set ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL).
A lock file stops two runs overlapping, and logs/run_history.csv records every run.







🧠 Prompt F9 — diagnose a failed run




[[Session primer.]] My pipeline run failed. Here is the console output: [[paste]], the last lines of logs/run_history.csv: [[paste]], and the failing test’s definition from tests/tests.yml: [[paste]]. Tell me whether this is a data problem (the source changed or delivered something wrong), a rule problem (my SQL or test is wrong) or an environment problem (files, permissions, connections). Give me the SQL to run against data/db/warehouse.failed.duckdb to confirm, and the message I should send to the data owner if it is their data.



✔ Check. The run ends with PUBLISHED. data/db/warehouse.duckdb and data/serve/mart.sqlite exist. Running it twice in a row gives the same numbers. Open mart.sqlite from Excel (Data → Get Data → From ODBC, with the SQLite ODBC driver) or Power BI to confirm the marts are usable.
💾 Commit: "First full run".

title: Appendix F — DIY prompt book: from your raw data to a live dashboard
text:
F.13 Stage 10 · The live dashboard
🎯 Goal: the interactive dashboard running on your own gold layer.
quarto serve dashboard.qmd
Your browser opens the dashboard. Nothing in it was written for your organisation: it builds its controls, filters, key performance indicator (KPI) cards and pages from semantic/metrics.yml and the warehouse.







Page
What it shows




Overview
Up to four KPI cards with the change against the previous period; a trend at the chosen grain (optionally split by the breakdown); a ranked breakdown


Explore
Every metric by the chosen breakdown, sortable, with CSV download


Data quality
The last run, the data on screen and when it was published, the latest test results, and what was loaded from where


Definitions
The metric definitions, owners and status, straight from metrics.yml



The sidebar holds the metric, the period, the time grain, the breakdown and a filter for every dimension. While the page is open it watches the warehouse file, and updates itself within refresh_seconds of a new publish.






Data quality: the gate’s results and the lineage, on the dashboard itself







Definitions: one definition per number, with its owner





Then make it yours:

Brand: change the colours and font in theme.scss, and the title in dashboard.qmd.
A page of your own: the generic pages cover most needs. For something specific, such as a marketing page from a mart, use this prompt.







🧠 Prompt F10 — add a page




[[Session primer, then attach ai_context.md and paste dashboard.qmd.]] Add a page called “[[name]]” to dashboard.qmd, after the Explore page, showing [[what, e.g. weekly spend and cost per conversion by channel from gold.mart_marketing_week]]. Follow the file’s conventions: query only through the existing q() helper (short-lived, read-only connections); call stamp() inside every render function so the page refreshes when the warehouse is republished; use the BRAND colours; take any metric definitions from M() rather than writing new formulas. Give me only the new page’s markdown and code, and say exactly where to paste it.



✔ Check. All pages load without error boxes. Filters change every chart and the KPI cards. The CSV download matches the table. The Data quality page shows the run you just made.
💾 Commit: "Dashboard customised".

section: F.14 Stage 11 · Publish it for colleagues
text:
F.14 Stage 11 · Publish it for colleagues
🎯 Goal: the people in your brief can open the dashboard in a browser, and nobody else can.








Option
When to choose it
How




Posit Connect (your organisation’s server)
Data must stay inside the organisation; sign-in with company accounts; scheduled refresh on the server
Rscript deploy.R connect, then schedule run_pipeline.R on the server (Stage 12)


Posit Connect Cloud
A quick, managed start; small teams
Rscript deploy.R connect, or Rscript deploy.R manifest and deploy from GitHub (only for data you may store in GitHub)


shinyapps.io
Demos and teaching
Rscript deploy.R shinyapps


A static version
No server allowed; an emailed or SharePoint pack
Export small cubes and render a static Quarto dashboard (Chapter 13)


The SQLite mart
Users live in Excel or Power BI
Share data/serve/mart.sqlite through the ODBC driver, or schedule a copy to a shared drive (Chapter 12)









🧠 Prompt F11 — choose and set up hosting




[[Session primer.]] Help me publish the dashboard. Constraints: [[who must see it; whether data may leave our network; what IT already runs (Posit Connect? Azure? a Linux server?); budget; sign-in requirements]]. Recommend one option from: Posit Connect, Posit Connect Cloud, shinyapps.io, a static dashboard, or the SQLite mart for Excel and Power BI users. Explain why, then give me numbered steps: one-time account setup, the deploy.R command, how to restrict access to named people, and how the data will be refreshed after publishing.



✔ Check. A colleague named in the brief can open the address and sees the same numbers as you. Someone not on the list cannot. The “Warehouse built” time at the bottom of the sidebar changes after the next scheduled run.
💾 Commit: "Deployment settings" (never commit account tokens; rsconnect/ is already in .gitignore).

section: F.15 Stage 12 · Schedule, monitor and alert
text:
F.15 Stage 12 · Schedule, monitor and alert
🎯 Goal: the pipeline runs itself, and people hear about failures before anyone sees a wrong number.
schedule/README.md gives ready-made entries for cron (macOS and Linux), Windows Task Scheduler, GitHub Actions and Posit Connect. For alerts, create an incoming webhook in a Microsoft Teams or Slack channel and put its address in .Renviron as ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL.






🧠 Prompt F12 — schedule it on my machine




[[Session primer.]] I want run_pipeline.R to run every [[weekday at 06:15 Lagos time]] on [[a Windows server / a Mac / a Linux virtual machine / Posit Connect]]. My project folder is [[path]] and R is installed at [[path, if known]]. Give me the exact steps and the scheduler entry, how to make sure it runs when nobody is logged in, where its output will be logged, and how to test it today without waiting until tomorrow.



✔ Check. The next morning, logs/run_history.csv has a new line with published = TRUE. Break a raw file on purpose once: the alert reaches the channel, and the dashboard keeps showing the last good data, stamped with its publish time.
💾 Commit: "Scheduled".

title: Appendix F — DIY prompt book: from your raw data to a live dashboard
text:
F.16 Stage 13 · Secure and govern
🎯 Goal: the platform meets your data-protection duties, and the numbers have owners.
Work through this list with your data protection officer (DPO) and the metric owners. The detail is in Chapter 15.

Classify each source as public, internal, confidential or restricted/personal, and record it next to the source in sources.yml as a comment.
Minimise: silver drops every column the brief doesn’t need. Personal identifiers are pseudonymised in silver (a consistent token, such as a hash with a secret salt kept in .Renviron), so gold has no names, phone numbers, Bank Verification Numbers (BVNs) or National Identification Numbers (NINs).
AI context: if raw data is personal, ai_context_samples: false in config.yml, so no example values leave your machine. Only use AI tools your organisation has approved.
Secrets are only in .Renviron (or the server’s secret store). git log -p | grep -i password finds nothing.
Access: the dashboard is restricted to named people or groups; the raw folder and the warehouse file sit on storage only the platform’s service account can read.
Retention: decide how long raw files are kept, and delete older ones on a schedule.
Accountability: a data protection impact assessment (DPIA) exists if the data is personal and the use is high-risk (profiling, scoring individuals). Each certified metric has an owner who has signed it off.







🧠 Prompt F13 — review my project for data-protection risk




[[Session primer, then attach ai_context.md, config.yml and sources.yml, with no secrets.]] Review this project against the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 principles (lawful basis and purpose, minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity and confidentiality, accountability). List every table or column that is likely personal or sensitive; say whether it should be dropped, pseudonymised or masked, and in which layer; and list what I must confirm with our DPO. Don’t give legal conclusions; give me the questions to ask.



✔ Check. Every box above is ticked or has a named person and a date next to it.

title: Appendix F — DIY prompt book: from your raw data to a live dashboard
text:
F.17 Stage 14 · Extensions (optional)
Once the core is running, each of these is one more stage of the same loop:

Ask your data. Add a page where people type a question, an AI writes SQL against gold.v_dashboard and the metric definitions, a person reviews it, and it runs read-only with a row cap. The guardrails are in Chapter 11; ask the AI to build it using the kit’s q() and M().
Search text by meaning. Complaints, reviews or exit-interview comments become a vector index next to the gold layer (Chapter 11).
Write-back. Targets or corrections entered in a Power Apps form (Dataverse) or a PostgreSQL app become a new source in sources.yml. Data still flows one way (Chapter 12).
More official data. World Bank, IMF, UN Comtrade, UNCTAD and Nigerian sources, as APIs in sources.yml (Appendix D).
A second subject area. Add facts that share your dimensions (a bus matrix), and a second view and metrics.yml model for another dashboard.

title: Appendix F — DIY prompt book: from your raw data to a live dashboard
text:
F.18 Definition of done

Rscript run_pipeline.R runs unattended on a schedule, and ends in PUBLISHED.
Every certified metric reconciles to its authoritative source, and that reconciliation is a test in the gate.
A broken delivery is caught by the gate, alerts a named person, and never reaches the dashboard.
The people in the brief use the dashboard, and the numbers they quote in meetings come from it.
Definitions, owners and data protection decisions are written down, in metrics.yml, docs/issues.md and the DPIA.
Everything except data and secrets is in Git, and a colleague could rebuild the platform from it on a new machine with 00_setup.R, the raw files, .Renviron and one run.

text:
F.19 Troubleshooting by stage








Symptom
Likely cause
Fix




there is no package called …
Setup incomplete
Re-run Rscript 00_setup.R; read the first error


A file is missing from bronze
Unsupported extension, or a hidden or temporary file (a name starting with ~$ or .)
Save as CSV or Excel workbook (XLSX); close the file in Excel; rename it


Columns called ...2, ...3
Title rows above the header
skip: in sources.yml (Stage 2)


â‚¦ instead of ₦
File saved in a legacy encoding
encoding: latin1 in sources.yml, or save as “CSV UTF-8”


ERROR for a database source
Driver, network or credentials
Check .Renviron names match sources.yml; test the connection in R; ask IT about firewalls


API source says ok (cached copy)
The API was unreachable; last good copy used
Fine for a day; check the URL, key or quota if it persists


Conversion Error in silver
A value that won’t cast
Use TRY_CAST and quarantine; find the value with the AI’s proof query


Gold has more rows than expected
Fan-out: joining on a key that isn’t unique
Check dimension uniqueness tests; aggregate before joining


Reconciliation test fails
Real difference, period mismatch, or a rule not applied
Compare month by month; don’t loosen the tolerance without the owner


Another run is in progress
A previous run was interrupted
Make sure no run is active, then delete data/db/.lock


Dashboard says “No dashboard data yet”
No published warehouse, or metrics.yml points at a missing view
Run the full pipeline; check model.table


Dashboard numbers didn’t change after a run
The gate closed, so the old data is still live
Check the Data quality page and logs/alerts.log
